name: General Sherman Tree Trail
quote: General Sherman Tree Trail | 1.0 miles 1.6 km | Sherman Tree Parking Lot or Shuttle Stop  [column headed 'Roundtrip Distance']
why: Short descending walk from the main lot to the General Sherman Tree.

name: Congress Trail (loop)
quote: Congress Trail (loop) | 2.7 miles 4.3 km | Sherman Tree Parking Lot or Shuttle Stop
why: Paved loop from the Sherman Tree through the heart of the Giant Forest sequoia grove.

name: Tokopah Falls Trail
quote: Tokopah Falls Trail | 3.8 miles 6.1 km | Trailhead across road bridge from Lodgepole Campground parking lot
why: Easy walk up the Marble Fork of the Kaweah from Lodgepole to a 1,200 ft cascading waterfall.

name: Crescent Meadow
quote: This trail is about 1.8 miles round trip.
why: Walk around Crescent Meadow among sequoias, on to Tharp's Log at Log Meadow and the Chimney Tree.

name: Big Trees Trail (loop)
quote: Big Trees Trail (loop) | 1.1 miles 1.8 km | Giant Forest Museum Parking Lot, or accessible lot
why: Paved, accessible loop around Round Meadow with sequoia-ecology panels.

name: Little Baldy Trail
quote: the Little Baldy Trail climbs 1.7 miles (2.7 km) along steep switchbacks, gaining 1,000 feet (300 m) in elevation.
why: Switchbacking climb near Dorst Campground to the top of a granite dome.

name: Muir Grove
quote: The mid-sized Muir Grove in Sequoia National Park is a two-mile hike from the parks' Generals Highway
why: Less-visited hike from near Dorst Creek Campground to a dense grove of mature sequoias.

name: Marble Falls Trail
quote: This trail climbs 3.9 miles (6km) through chaparral to a lovely cascade.
why: Foothills climb from Potwisha Campground through chaparral to a waterfall.

name: Middle Fork Trail
quote: Panther Creek Falls is 3 miles (5 km) from the parking area.
why: Foothills trail along the Middle Fork of the Kaweah with Moro Rock views, to Panther Creek Falls.

name: Lady Bug Trail
quote: The trail ends 3 miles (5 km) near one of the lowest-elevation sequoia groves.
why: Moderately steep hike along the South Fork of the Kaweah to a low-elevation sequoia grove.

name: Garfield Grove Trail
quote: This trail is a relatively steep 5-mile (8.3 km) one-way climb to the Garfield Sequoia Grove.
why: Steep climb from South Fork Campground to the Garfield sequoia grove.

name: Monarch Lakes
quote: Upper and Lower Monarch Lakes lie at the foot of Sawtooth Peak, at the end of a 4.2 mile (one-way) hike.
why: Mineral King hike through Chihuahua Bowl to two lakes below Sawtooth Peak.

name: Timber Gap
quote: The hike to Timber Gap is 2 miles one-way.
why: Old mining route from Mineral King up to a red-fir-covered gap with views to Alta Peak.

name: White Chief Trail
quote: The 2.9 mile one-way trail to the White Chief Bowl is a steep but scenic hike up the west side of the Mineral King Valley.
why: Steep climb past Crabtree's cabin ruins to White Chief Bowl.

name: Eagle and Mosquito Lakes (Eagle Lake)
quote: The left-hand trail goes to Eagle Lake, a glacially carved tarn 3.4 miles (one way) from the trailhead.
why: Steady climb up the west side of Mineral King Valley to a glacial tarn.

name: Eagle and Mosquito Lakes (Mosquito Lake #1)
quote: The right-hand trail ends at Mosquito Lake #1, 3.6 miles (one way) from the trailhead
why: Shares the Eagle Lake trail, then forks right to the first Mosquito Lake.

name: Crystal Lake
quote: The trail to Crystal Lake (4.9 miles one-way) branches off of the Monarch Lakes Trail at Chihuahua Bowl
why: Steep branch off the Monarch Lakes trail past old mine remnants to a dammed lake.

name: Franklin Lakes
quote: Although the 5.4 mile one-way hike can be done as a day trip
why: Mineral King hike past colourful metamorphic rock to lakes below Franklin Pass.
